title: Paired neutrophil association and ex vivo perturbation sensitivity define a bounded myeloid activation model in ARDS
content:
by Wei Wei, Jing Liu, Ying Zhou, Rui Zhao, LinGang Zhang

Background

Acute respiratory distress syndrome (ARDS) is biologically heterogeneous, but how myeloid transcriptional programmes relate across blood and lung compartments remains uncertain. We examined whether a pre-specified neutrophil effector/degranulation programme and a separately derived perturbation-response module provide convergent, boundary-aware evidence across public cohorts.

Methods

Patient-level analyses descriptively localized programmes in a seven-patient peripheral blood mononuclear cell cohort and assessed paired bronchoalveolar lavage fluid and longitudinal alveolar-macrophage profiles. PBMC disease groups were severely confounded with expression-inferred sex. In purified neutrophils, paired ARDS–healthy-volunteer comparisons and healthy-donor granulocyte–macrophage colony-stimulating factor (GM-CSF)/broad phosphoinositide 3-kinase (PI3K) perturbations were analysed separately. A donor-adjusted whole-transcriptome weighted gene coexpression network analysis (WGCNA) derived a module under frozen retention rules, which was externally projected using fixed loadings and a pre-specified coverage gate.

Results

The neutrophil-degranulation programme was higher in all 12 ARDS–healthy-volunteer pairs (mean paired difference, 0.0321; Benjamini–Hochberg false-discovery rate [BH-FDR] = 0.000977), increased after GM-CSF in 9 of 10 donors (BH-FDR = 0.0276) and decreased after broad pan-PI3K inhibition in all 10 donors (BH-FDR = 0.00469). No gene passed the genome-wide three-direction conjunction threshold; SERPINB1, PNP and TLR2 were retained only as pathway-restricted directional response anchors. A separate 627-gene green module met the perturbation-response rule (conjunction BH-FDR = 3.50 × 10⁻⁴) and showed functional convergence with limited gene-level overlap. PBMC localization was descriptive, without an interpretable ARDS–sepsis contrast. External green projection showed post hoc monocyte/macrophage-biased ordering rather than neutrophil specificity. In eight paired BALF patients, the pre-specified contrast was directionally opposite but inconclusive (P = 0.571); longitudinal outcome evidence was inconsistent.

Conclusions

These data support an ARDS-associated myeloid/neutrophil effector programme with paired disease association and ex vivo GM-CSF/pan-PI3K sensitivity. They support mechanistic prioritization of compartment-dependent myeloid biology, but not a prognostic signature, a causal programme-to-outcome mechanism, PI3K isoform specificity or PI3K-directed therapeutic efficacy.
